source.summary: Primary object is the black wired Lenovo mouse on white background (image-1). Visible components include domed top housing, left/right click surfaces separated by red scroll wheel, and thin black cable exiting front. Scope is the mouse only; background and cable beyond frame are not counted as components.

parts.name: Main top housing / palm dome
parts.evidence: Matte black domed shell tapering toward front, white 'lenovo' text on rear slope, glossy side wall visible on left flank
parts.role: Houses internal electronics and provides ergonomic surface for hand; likely supports buttons and wheel

parts.name: Red scroll wheel
parts.evidence: Small red ridged wheel set in central slot between click surfaces near front
parts.role: May rotate to scroll content and possibly press as middle button; not proven in still photo

parts.name: Left click surface
parts.evidence: Smooth panel to left of wheel slot extending from front edge toward middle
parts.role: Likely depresses to actuate a switch for left-click when pressed

parts.name: Right click surface
parts.evidence: Smooth panel to right of wheel slot, mirror of left side
parts.role: Likely depresses to actuate a switch for right-click when pressed

parts.name: Wired cable
parts.evidence: Thin black flexible cord exiting front center, snaking toward top of frame out of view
parts.role: May carry power and data between mouse and computer; exact connector not visible

parts.name: Rear palm rest and logo area
parts.evidence: Rounded rear of housing with white 'lenovo' branding on matte surface
parts.role: Supports palm and identifies manufacturer; no functional electronics inferred from logo alone

parts.name: Left side wall / side grip
parts.evidence: Slightly glossy vertical side curving under top dome, visible due to perspective
parts.role: Provides thumb rest and side enclosure

problem: Hypothetical integration-test symptom, not a verified defect: the red scroll wheel feels sticky while other buttons work. Only suggest external cleaning, no disassembly.

assessment.summary: User reports hypothetical sticky feel of red scroll wheel while other buttons work. No verified damage in original scan photo; photo shows wheel in place. Cautious external cleaning only is appropriate, no disassembly.

evidence.basis: Red scroll wheel visible in central slot between click surfaces, appears seated with no photographed damage or missing parts
User-reported symptom: red scroll wheel feels sticky while left/right click surfaces work - text report, not visually verifiable and described as hypothetical integration-test, not a verified defect
Main top housing matte black dome appears intact around wheel slot, no visible spill residue in this overhead view

alternatives.reason: General dust or residue on top housing around wheel slot could contribute to sticky feel without internal failure
Left click surface unlikely given report that other buttons work, but included to show wheel-specific symptom isolation

steps.title: Disconnect for safe external work
steps.instruction: Unplug the wired mouse from the computer and place it upside-down on a clean dry white surface in good light.
steps.check: Confirm cable is disconnected before touching wheel area
steps.stopIf: Stop if cable is frayed, connector damaged, or housing is cracked

steps.title: Inspect wheel slot externally
steps.instruction: Look closely at the red scroll wheel and the narrow slot edges for visible lint or surface dust without inserting tools or opening housing.
steps.check: Note whether any dust is visible around wheel rims
steps.stopIf: Stop if wheel is loose, detached, or housing is broken

steps.title: Gentle external dry cleaning
steps.instruction: With mouse still unplugged and angled downward, lightly wipe housing and gently sweep around wheel with a clean dry soft brush or dry lint-free cloth to dislodge surface dust.
steps.check: Observe if wheel looks cleaner and rolls slightly more freely with gentle finger roll
steps.stopIf: Stop if wheel binds, grinds, or resistance increases

steps.title: Reconnect and verify lightly
steps.instruction: Plug mouse back in and test scroll with normal light finger motion only.
steps.check: Check whether stickiness is reduced during normal use
steps.stopIf: Stop further attempts if stickiness persists and seek manufacturer guidance rather than disassembling

precautions: Keep all liquids away from mouse and do not spray cleaners directly onto wheel
Do not disassemble, pry wheel, remove housing, or insert pins/tools into slot
Use only gentle dry wiping; do not force wheel or apply excessive pressure
limitations: Symptom is user-reported and hypothetical per problem description, not photographically verified; internal mechanical wear cannot be confirmed from still photo
External cleaning cannot address internal switch or axle damage; no diagnosis of confirmed fault is made
Safe operation is not promised; persistent stickiness needs manufacturer support or qualified service

notice: AI-suggested fault and repair guidance, not a verified diagnosis. No photos are stored on the server.
